#2018. Didier Deschamps 'doesn't want Manchester United job': Blow for Sir Jim Ratcliffe as unemployed former France boss appears hesitant to replace under-fire Michael Carrick

Published: 04:37 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 04:37 EST, 6 November 2026

Manchester United have suffered a road bump in sounding out potential replacements for Michael Carrick – as Didier Deschamps reportedly doesn't want the gig.

Deschamps, who left the France job after 14 years following the World Cup, has told the club he is uninterested according to the Daily Mirror.

Carrick remains in post but his bosses have been privately talking to possible successors for weeks after an abysmal start to the season which has left them 17th in the Premier League.

Eddie Howe, Fabian Hurzeler, Unai Emery and Antonio Conte have all come up on the shortlist, with the international break this month seen as an ideal time for managerial changes across the league.

Deschamps appealed to United because of his immediate availability and lack of a compensation fee, but is in no rush to take a job and snubbed their advance.

After a glittering career as a player, he has won the World Cup managing France, lifted Ligue 1 with Marseille, led Monaco to a Champions League final, and got Juventus promoted back to Serie A after the Calciopoli scandal.

Didier Deschamps has reportedly told Manchester United he is not interested in the job

Michael Carrick remains in post but United have been sounding out potential replacements for weeks

Carrick's prospects of keeping the job had a boost on Tuesday as Matheus Cunha struck two late goals to produce a stunning turnaround win against Roma in the Champions League.

But he only has a clash against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday afternoon before the international break to prove to the hierarchy that he should keep his job.

That comeback against Roma stopped a rot which has been spreading for weeks. United were on the verge of going ten games without a win, a run unprecedented in the club's history.

They have reached a nadir in recent weeks after batterings by Como and Bournemouth – the latter at Old Trafford, no less – while players have been openly mutinous.

Bruno Fernandes publicly criticised Carrick's tactics after the 4-1 defeat at Como, leading to Carrick benching him for the next game against Bournemouth.

And Lisandro Martinez has singled out director of football Jason Wilcox over United's transfer activity, suggesting the squad was left short on quality after the transfer window.

Were Carrick to go, it is unclear who would replace him.

Emery is open to signing a new deal with Aston Villa which would take him to close to a decade at the club, and held a meeting with club chiefs on Wednesday.

Hurzeler does not have a release clause in his Brighton contract and so would require enormous compensation. There is well-placed scepticism as to whether any move would even be remotely possible, regardless of how well liked he is inside Old Trafford.

Nagelsmann and Conte are both out of work and the latter has previously indicated that he would like the challenge of restoring a fallen giant to glory.

#2017. Rangers icon Scott Arfield turns to Michael Beale after landing East Fife job

He broke through at Falkirk when John Hughes was in charge, played for five years under Sean Dyche at Burnley, helped Steven Gerrard to lift the Scottish title at Rangers, was a member of the Giovanni van Bronckhorst side that reached the Europa League final and starred as John McGlynn steered his first club back into the Premiership.

So Scott Arfield, who was officially unveiled as the new player-manager of William Hill League One outfit East Fife at New Bayview this afternoon, has no shortage of top-class coaches to turn to for advice about how to succeed in the dugout in the months ahead.

It was something of a surprise, then, when the midfielder revealed who he has contacted since agreeing to take over from the inimitable Dick Campbell in the Methil hotseat and who he hopes to emulate going forward.

“I have spoken to previous managers,” he said. “The one I have spoken to the most and as recently as last night is John Hughes. He has worked in part-time football before so he knows everything about it. I have known him since I was 15 and he has been giving me great pointers.

“But Michael Beale is definitely another one. He was the first person I spoke to when I got the job at Livingston (Arfield was appointed caretaker at Almondvale towards the end of last season). He is the same as John. He worked in academy football at Liverpool and Chelsea. He gave me an analysis.”

Beale, despite being first-team coach under Gerrard when Rangers were crowned Scottish champions for the first time in 10 years in 2021, is hardly held in high regard by fans of the Ibrox club these days.

The Englishman, who is now at Zulte Waregem in Belgium, struggled when he was manager in Govan and was sacked after less than a year in the role. However, he left a lasting impression on one player who became a firm favourite with supporters during his time with his boyhood heroes.

So what was it that Arfield liked about working with him? “His variety,” he said. “I was down at Burnley for five years, where they had a brilliant management team. But it was very structured in terms of Monday to Friday and how you prepared for games and debriefed a game.

“Mick perhaps didn’t have the reputation at that time. Steven was the authority figure. I wouldn’t say he was in the background as such. He was looking over things from a vantage point. But Mick was hands-on.

“His variability and ability to make everyone enthused and involved in the drill was just incredible. His knowledge of football and the variety of his training drills was amazing. It didn’t matter if you were a left-back or a centre-forward, everyone was all in, switched on and really focused on the training drills. That was my lasting impression.”

New East Fife player-manager Scott Arfield at New Bayview today (Image: Mark Runnacles / Shutterstock)

Arfield added, “He was absolutely delighted when I phoned him. He knows you cannot just go in at the top. There’s so many players who have gone from my position and even higher (into lower-tier teams). There’s very few players who can go straight in (at a high level).

“Look at Steven Gerrard, one of the most iconic footballers there’s ever been. He had to go into an academy at first. He was obviously willing to go into an academy and actually sit there looking at kids progressing. He got experience and then came up and won a league in Scotland with the help of Mick.

“Mick was delighted when I called him. He completely and utterly understands Scottish football at all levels because of the cup games we were involved in down the years. He knows it is a great situation. I think I am one of the first to get into management from that core group, so he is delighted to see it happen.”

Arfield also intends to get in touch with Gerrard, who took to Instagram yesterday to congratulate his former charge on his appointment at East Fife, in the coming days.

He admitted there are aspects of the legendary Liverpool and England captain’s management style that he will be borrowing in the weeks and months ahead.

"I certainly will be picking his brains,” he said. “I loved Steven's calmness as a manager. I absolutely loved it. When he spoke, people listened. I thought his demeanour was (fantastic).

“There were so many times he could have lost his head, but I think if you do that, if you're too emotional, players sometimes switch off, especially in this day and age. So the calm, authoritative figure is something that I'll be trying to keep.

“It does not matter at what level you are at, you need to get the best out of players. It is an important trait. It could be the most important thing you have got. I think I can get people on board and progress their football career and their ability.”

Arfield got a brief taste of management last season when he took over from Marvin Bartley at Livingston on an interim basis for the final three games of a difficult season. He was pleased to discover that he revelled in the position.

“I just loved everything about it,” he said. “I loved the chaos of it. I loved getting thrown into it. I have spoken to so many ex-players who have told me they thought they would want it and then when they got thrown into it found they didn’t want it.

Scott Arfield is unveiled as the new player-manager of East Fife (Image: Mark Runnacles / Shutterstock)

“It went the opposite way with me. It just ignited something in me that I knew was in there. But I didn’t know how big the fire was. When I was looking back over the summer at all these valuable experiences - dictating things, coming in at half-time and trying to assess the problems, seeing it from a completely different side from playing – I recognised that it ignited something in me.

“I was just waiting for the right opportunity. I didn’t want to rush into any opportunity, hence the reason why I am here in November. It is the perfect scenario and hopefully I can repay the faith that East Fife showed in me.”

Following in the footsteps of Campbell, one of the most successful lower-league managers in Scottish football history, will not be easy. But Arfield, who intends to play when he gets his match fitness and sharpness up to the required level, is undaunted by the prospect.

“I have never crossed paths with Dick,” he said. “But I have met loads of players throughout my career who have great stories about him. Listen, we have probably got different ideas about how the game should be played. But there is one ball and two goals.

“Belief in players is a big thing. You see it everywhere in Scottish football. If somebody can come in and give you a different dimension it is a good thing. There will be players here who will probably not be able to do what I am asking. They will find it tough. But I need to assess the team. Everybody is on a blank canvas.

“Whether they are good enough, whether I will need to bring players in in January to get to where I am wanting to go, we will see. The previous management team thought the players were good enough for their style. But it will be a different style.

“Obviously I will be telling the players what I demand and expect. But I will still tell them to play here how they would play with their mates – with that freedom. Football is an entertainment business and I want players to enjoy it.”

Arfield is optimistic that his contacts in the Scottish and English game, including at Rangers, will be invaluable to him if he feels that he has to strengthen his squad at East Fife during the January transfer window.

“I remember when I was at Falkirk first time around,” he said. “Yogi [Hughes] and Brian Rice at Falkirk travelled all about the country with not a big budget whatsoever. They were ducking and diving a bit like Del Boy to try and get the best deals. So that'll be my thought process, to recruit the best players.

“The best thing you can give young players is a platform to perform and get eyes on them. Under-23 football down the road and reserve team and B team football just doesn't quite give you what men's football gives you.

Scott Arfield is unveiled as the new player-manager of East Fife by chairman Liam Anderson (Image: Mark Runnacles / Shutterstock)

“So, that's obviously the scenario. That's why teams with high hopes for their prospects give them to teams like this - to put eyes on them and to get their talents growing at a faster rate than what they would get. I'll certainly be trying to use my contacts for the best players.”

Arfield continued, “We've got these Hearts boys (Connor Dow and Liam Walker) here, but they’re not getting enough eyes on them and they’re not growing. So Hearts are obviously going to be thinking, ‘Why are we giving you these players where we could just keep them training here?’.

“There's no obligation on me to play them, but they're at Hearts for a reason. They'll certainly have a point to prove with me. As I say, they're obviously there for a reason. Whether they can get up to a physicality to play in this league is a different matter.

“But the technical ability is there. That's another thing I need to look at - to see if they're good enough to put the current team out.”

#2016. Liverpool star’s agent confirms talks are underway over prospective new contract

The agent of one Liverpool player has confirmed that ‘preliminary talks’ are underway over a prospective new contract at Anfield for his client.

There has been much speculation in recent months regarding the long-term future of Alexis Mac Allister, who’s voiced his dismay at not being offered a new deal by the club earlier this year.

However, another South American stalwart in Alisson Becker revealed over the past couple of days that he’d be happy to remain on Merseyside beyond the expiry of his current terms next June.

The goalkeeper’s agent Ze Maria has indicated that negotiations over a contract renewal for the 34-year-old have commenced (albeit at an early stage) and that the Brazil international is very keen to remain with Liverpool.

Alisson’s representative told Egyptian news outlet WinWin: “Alisson loves Liverpool very much. We are in preliminary talks to renew the contract.”

(Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Following on from the Reds’ number 1 expressing his desire to extend his contract, this claim from his agent represents another positive sign that the veteran stopper will continue with LFC beyond next summer.

The Brazilian has been world-class throughout his eight-and-a-bit years at Anfield so far and, despite a couple of costly errors in recent games, was back to his exceptional best in the weekend victory over Crystal Palace as he pulled off a string of fantastic saves.

Liverpool tend not to hand out lucrative contract renewals to players in their mid-30s, but just as they made an exception for Mo Salah in April 2025, we wouldn’t rule out them doing the same for Alisson if he continues to exept.

The goalkeeper is currently on £250,000 per week, with only six of his teammates earning more at present (Capology), so it’d likely require another significant financial commitment to keep him at the club for another season or two.

It’ll likely take another few months before we know for certain whether or not he’ll still be a Reds player next term, but for now the indications are positive that we won’t have to say farewell to the legendary ‘keeper in six months’ time and can instead look forward to even more brilliance from him at Anfield after that.

#2014. Cherki magic helping Maresca to step out of Guardiola shadow

Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

They swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under new manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

City created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

Erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

However, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

An insight into Cherki’s mindset came after the match.

He said: “My performance is s---. In the first half, we didn’t find the space, I played bad. I need to show them that I want to play, I want to score. Next time I want to give the ball around more.”

Forget the words, Maresca cannot ignore the actions of a player he left on the bench against Bournemouth.

Sterner tests will come for City than against a Palace side missing key players who may or may not leave south London in the remaining days of the transfer window.

Whether Maresca will trust his forward players to express themselves as freely against their rivals for the Premier League title remains to be seen, but with Elliot Anderson providing a one-man shield behind them, City could not be stopped.

Maresca said: “For sure Rayan is happy tonight. His performance was very good and not just for his two goals. He has to press off the ball and he was in charge of [marking] Adam Wharton, so it was a complete game by him.”

Only for the first three minutes did Palace hint at a different outcome but, after shots from Eddie Nketiah and Daichi Kamada were diverted away for corners, City took control.

They took the lead in the 17th minute when the otherwise quiet Antoine Semenyo flighted a cross over the heads of everyone except the shorn locks of Haaland, whose determined header looped over Henderson and dropped in the far corner.

The only negative of Foden’s performance came in front of goal, with a ballooned shot and a mistimed header.

After Cherki’s solo masterpiece had made it 2-0, Yeremy Pino seized the next moment for his own with a stunning free-kick that flicked the crossbar, then the back of City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma before finally dropping over the line.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Whatever hope that mustered was snatched away again when Cherki scored his second goal and the third goal of a breathless five minutes.

His shot at the end of a darting run flicked the ankle of Tomiyasu to send it just out of Henderson’s reach.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Morocco teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi had little time to show why City have paid Lille £85.6m for him with a late entry as a substitute, but they didn’t need him on this occasion.

Foden then set off on a swerving run that set up Haaland to lash home his second goal of the game and make it 4-1.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF

The fear for Palace is that they cannot keep selling their best players and expecting to replicate the success on the pitch that has brought them three trophies in the past 15 months.

Leicester City offer a shuddering example of that. From Premier League champions to League One in 10 seasons.

Pierre Sage, the new Palace manager, will welcome the certainty that the closure of the transfer window will bring, particularly over the futures of forwards Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, as well as wing-back Daniel Muñoz.

The one player he cannot afford to lose is Wharton, who matched the City midfield on his own at times in the first half.

Sage said: “I think the score is heavy. We stayed in the game for 65 minutes and created some chances. We know we are in for a tough season, but we have created a lot of opportunities in the first two games.

“I could speak about the transfer window, but I don’t want to find an excuse. We just have to be sure that in four days’ time, the team will be better than today.”

“It has been a short pre-season. Rayan [Cherki], five weeks ago was at the World Cup. Game by game, we will be back, just need a few games. We played well, it is a new manager but we have been playing together, with the addition of a few new players. We know what to do and have to trust the system.”

“We have to keep on playing together, find out where we are best and how to play. We have so many good players and we have to fit everyone in. He has to keep going because we know how good Phil is, it is about showing it week in week out. This is the right step forward for everyone. We have to build on this.”

"I'm just trying to play my football" 💪Elliot Anderson is excited about the future at Manchester City after his summer transfer 🔥 pic.twitter.com/huGv4Li3GZ

"Say what you actually mean!" 🤣Erling Haaland takes over Rayan Cherki's post-match interview! pic.twitter.com/adW6IU8DzQ

2 + 2 - Rayan Cherki is the third player to have a game with multiple goals and another game with multiple assists across a team's first two matches of a Premier League campaign, after Thierry Henry in 2004-05 and Didier Drogba in 2010-11.Polymath. pic.twitter.com/4cRV0xMIFa

September 5: Fulham vs Crystal PalaceSeptember 12: Crystal Palace vs IpswichSeptember 19: Leeds vs Crystal PalaceOctober 11: Crystal Palace vs Nottingham ForestOctober 18: Brighton vs Crystal Palace

Pierre Sage’s side will host Middlesbrough in the League Cup third round next month and will also begin their Europa League campaign in September.

The directions of these teams will be diverging this season. City were wonderful, free-flowing, expressive and fun to watch. Palace not so much. It will take Pierre Sage a while to impose his style of play. It will certainly take another week before he knows his final squad for the first half of the season.

It was noticeable at the final whistle that many Palace fans stayed around to applaud Daniel Munoz, an unused substitute on the night, as he made his way to the tunnel, probably for the final time as a Palace player if Nottingham Forest’s interest in him becomes a transfer by the end of the window.

"Cherki was the difference" 🪄"He is a genius" 🧠Jamie Redknapp reacts to Crystal Palace 1-4 Man City 🔊 pic.twitter.com/UjSarMngDR

Manchester City will take on Norwich in the League Cup third round in September and will also have their first Champions League match next month.

Possession: Crystal Palace 28%-72% Manchester CityShots: 9-18Shots on target: 1-9Corners: 2-6Touches in the opposition box: 13-33

Pretty comprehensive in Manchester City’s favour, which is reflected in the scoreline.

The final whistle is blown at Selhurst Park and Manchester City have cruised to a 4-1 win thanks to doubles from Cherki and Haaland. Enzo Maresca’s side make it two wins from two whereas it is two defeats from two for Pierre Sage.

Manchester City, with the three points already in the bag, are just stroking the ball around with ease and are in complete control. Palace can barely get a foot on it.

A late double substitution for Manchester City as Reis and Braithwaite come on. Enzo Maresca’s side are cruising to victory to make it two wins from two.

Cherki has two goals to his name and now Haaland does as Manchester City are romping to victory in south London. Guehi wins possession for City inside the Palace half and the ball comes to Foden, who dribbles towards the Palace penalty area. He lays it off to his left to Haaland who, from a narrow angle, finds the root of the net.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF

Nearly an instant impact from McAidoo as the 18-year-old drives through the Palace half and curls a shot from the edge of the box that goes just wide.

When Manchester City were making those substitutions, the Crystal Palace fans were making sure they let the officials know how long the Manchester City players were taking to get off.

There is going to be a debut for the Premier League’s most expensive teenager ever as Bouaddi comes on for Manchester City. McAidoo is also coming on, with Cherki and Anderson going off.

Mingueza eventually comes on but not after having to wait until the ball goes out of play again as Khalaili was adjudged to have taken too long to have got off the pitch. Safe to say the Palace fans are not too impressed with that new rule. It will probably be a pub question in the years ahead. That change does mean that Palace have used all five substitutions, which means Munoz will not come on. He is being linked with a reunion with Oliver Glasner at Nottingham Forest in the final days of this window.

Crystal Palace make another double change and it will be two debuts as Disasi and Mingueza come on.

Enzo Maresca turns to his bench for the first time tonight as Kovacic comes on.

Khalaili brings down Semenyo and is booked for that challenge.

Palace are going to make a double substitution as McNeil and Gozo replace Nketiah and Pino. 19-year-old Gozo is on for his Palace debut.

That was a chance for Palace. Guessand finds Pino, who drives into the Manchester City penalty area on the right. Pino has Nketiah at the far post but there is too much on the cross.

Guessand, back at Palace, is going to come on to replace Strand Larsen, who has been pretty quiet up top for the home side tonight.

Sometimes you feel blessed to witness an extraordinary moment of footballing genius. Selhurst Park has just seen two in the space of three minutes. Yeremy Pino’s free-kick which flicked off the back of Gianluigi Donnarumma was stunning, but even that could not truly compare to the slalom run of Rayan Cherki that drew a collective intake of breath from all those present. The Frenchman has just followed it with a scorching shot. It couldn’t compare with his first, though.

Three goals come in quick succession and Cherki restores Manchester City’s two-goal advantage with his second of the night. The Frenchman receives it on the turn from around 30 yards out and drives towards the Palace penalty area. He then shoots and a kind deflection off Richards takes it over Henderson’s diving effort and into the Palace net.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Just as the hosts appeared to maybe out of this one, they get a goal back. Pino’s fantastic free-kick strikes the bar, hits Donnarumma on the back before going into the net off the post. That hit the frame of the goal twice and Palace have a crucial goal, minutes after going 2-0 down.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Anderson brings down Pino not far outside the Manchester City penalty area and is booked.

The next goal in this game felt crucial and the visitors have it. Foden drives towards the Palace penalty area before playing a pass forward into the path of Cherki. The Frenchman has numerous defenders around but he shows neat footwork to skip past a few, holds off Richards before slotting home with his left foot.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

No-one has had fewer touches on the pitch tonight than Haaland up until this point but the Norwegian’s goal is the difference. His number of touches (14) is the joint fewest with his compatriot Strand Larsen.

That was a good chance for Nketiah. He plays the ball to the underlapping Mitchell, who from the byline cuts it back into the path of Nketiah. The former Arsenal man should so so much better with his opportunity from the edge of the six-yard box but fires a long way wide.

Semenyo wins Manchester City an early corner in this second half off Canvot. Anderson’s delivery beyond the back post picks out O’Reilly, who in space heads back across goal but Pino heads away.

We are back under way at Selhurst Park, with Manchester City carrying a 1-0 lead into this second half. As the players emerged from the tunnels for the second half, the DJ at Selhurst Park paid tribute to the late Dolly Parton and Kenny Rogers by playing Islands in the Stream. Nice touch! Get your favourite Dolly and Kenny tunes in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Possession: Crystal Palace 33%-67% Manchester CityShots: 7-11Shots on target: 1-6Corners: 2-2Touches in the opposition box: 10-18

The stats are certainly in Manchester City’s favour and they will feel they probably should have more than the one goal.

Cherki has a late chance for Manchester City but his shot is well saved by Henderson down to his right.

The first half at Selhurst Park is then brought to an end and Manchester City lead 1-0 at the break thanks to Haaland’s header.

There will be just one added minute at the end of this first half.

Palace started off with a nominal back three. That has become a back five far too often for Pierre Sage’s liking at times in this first half, yet still City are playing through them almost at will. The Palace fans whose deafening support accompanied Palace shots in the opening minutes are reduced to cheering battling midfield runs that win a free-kick now.

Pino delivers a free-kick into the Manchester City box and Richards gets to it first. It comes off his shoulder and rolls into the arms of Donnarumma.

Semenyo’s shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Richards, forcing Henderson into a decent save.

Palace now miss a big opportunity and should be on level terms. Wharton, who has probably been the best player on the pitch tonight, whips in a cross from the right and picks out Mitchell, who has a free header from eight yards out but somehow misses the target.

Strand Larsen comes close with a header from a Pino cross but he would have been offside anyway.

The first booking of the night goes the way of the visitors. Wharton drives forward into the Manchester City half and is cynically brought down by Cherki, who looked perplexed when the yellow card was shown but it was an obvious booking.

Foden wastes his second big chance of this first half. Manchester City break through O’Reilly, who carries it down the right. He waits for Cherki to make the overlapping run before passing to the Frenchman. Cherki’s cross picks out Foden inside the six-yard box and the latter should score but he gets a simple header all wrong.

Well, that was easy. So easy in fact – perfect Semenyo cross, perfect Haaland header - that it hushed Selhurst Park as the ball looped over Dean Henderson. Even the roar from the enclave of City fans took a moment to fill the south London air. You wouldn’t say that all the pre-match optimism among Palace fans has been punctured, but the home side need a moment if they aren’t to sink without trace to a City side bossing possession and territory now.

That is a huge miss from Foden. Anderson picks out his compatriot in acres of space on the right side of the box, with no Palace defender within five yards of him, but Foden blazes over the bar when he should have put Manchester City 2-0 up.

King Harald V of Norway has died in the last few days and over the last few hours two Norwegian cyclists claimed a one-two at the Vuelta a Espana and now Haaland has a goal.

He has barely touched the ball thus far but he puts the visitors ahead just past the quarter-of-an-hour mark. Semenyo is afforded too much space on the left just outside the penalty area and clips in a cross towards the far post. Haaland gets up highest, above Richards, and guides a superb header over Henderson into the Palace net.

Erling Haaland gets off the mark for the new Premier League season! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/5ZjQUVk6Zl

The England boss is in attendance tonight, perhaps keeping a close eye on that midfield battle between Anderson and Wharton.

Palace flirt with danger inside their own penalty area. After Haaland’s flick, Kamada should just belt the ball away but instead inexplicably leaves it. Henderson manages to mop up just as Foden was eyeing up the chance.

There is a mad scramble inside the Palace box but somehow the hosts escape without conceding. Initially, Anderson’s shot from range is saved by Henderson but Manchester City keep it alive in the penalty area. Palace frantically attempt to clear their lines and eventually they do after Haaland came close.

Quite a lot of the focus tonight will be on two English midfielders; one who has got a big-money move this summer and the other thus far has not. Anderson is directly up against Wharton and so far it is the latter who is winning the early battles, including dispossessing Anderson in midfield.

The first chance of the game goes the way of the hosts. It stems from a quite sensational first-time pass from Wharton from inside his own half into the left channel to pick out the run of Nketiah, whose shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Dias and is saved by Donnarumma.

Manchester City initially clear the corner but Palace keep it alive. Kamada’s shot from just inside the box appeared to be on target but it is headed over for another corner, which is easily caught by Donnarumma.

We are under way at Selhurst Park. Will Pierre Sage earn his first win as Palace boss or can Enzo Maresca and City make it two wins from two?

Both sides emerge from the tunnel in the corner of Selhurst Park to the customary sound of Glad All Over and we are moments away from kick-off in south London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Crystal Palace: Henderson, Khalaili, Canvot, Richards, Tomiyasu, Mitchell, Wharton, Kamada, Pino, Strand Larsen, Nketiah.Substitutes: Benitez, Munoz, Disasi, Mingueza, Hughes, Lerma, Gozo, McNeil, Guessand.

Manchester City: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly, Anderson, Guehi, Cherki, Foden Semenyo, Haaland.Substitutes: Rulli, Kovacic, Ait-Nouri, Reis, Echeverri, Bouaddi, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Lewis.

Yes! It may have been fleeting but the boy in the Palace tracksuit top had his moment after all with Erling Haaland as City waited in line to enter the Selhurst Park pitch. And having done so, he fairly skipped up the steps back with his dad back to their seats. Whether the boy’s second wish of the evening, for a Palace victory, will come true is another question altogether.

The young Palace fan is still waiting for Haaland. Another determined walk back to the dressing room. It isn’t a simple task to attract an opposition player’s attention when you are leaning over a barrier a few feet higher than him – and in the home end. Haaland and his teammates have the look of a team that knows it must perform tonight to ease the concerns that they are a team in transition. The City fans will not entertain such thoughts, either.

Crystal Palace looked set to sign Club Brugge defender Joel Ordonez but that deal could be in doubt as there may be some problems with his medical. We await to see further updates on that situation.

“He is a genius. Make no mistake. Managers now want structure, they do not like players who are a bit loose out of possession. But I go to football matches to watch people like him play.

“That is what makes me smile. I do not like watching players pass it sideways, that is not why I go to football. I go to watch geniuses do their work. Some managers will not appreciate it. But last week he got his manager out of a hole because without him they would not have won that game.”

"He's irreplaceable" 💥Jamie Redknapp and Clinton Morrison sing the praises of Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton 🤝 pic.twitter.com/ZOpcZcItHY

Jack Grealish is not in the Manchester City squad tonight amid links with the likes of Everton and Sunderland. Will he still be at the club beyond the deadline? It would appear not.

Both Ismaila Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta are out of the Crystal Palace squad tonight with injury but could they be on the move before the window slams shut? Sarr has been linked with Galatasaray and Liverpool whilst the situation is complicated with Mateta as he claims the final year of his contract is void. How do those two situations resolve themselves? Daniel Munoz has been linked with a move to Nottingham Forest but is on the bench for Palace this evening.

An unfulfilled wish so far for a young Palace fan holding up a child’s red Norway shirt with ‘Haaland’ emblazoned on it. Having waited patiently for the City players to emerge for their warm-up and being held by his dad as he leant over the stone wall to attract Haaland’s attention, he was left disappointed because the City striker was simply not looking as he and his teammates jogged past. Will the boy, who has on a Palace tracksuit top, get a photo with his hero when the striker returns to the Portakabin that hosts the away dressing room prior to kick-off? Stay tuned.

"The results will certainly come" ✅Dean Henderson urges patience as Crystal Palace go through a transitional period under new manager Pierre Sage 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/1pJjRPeKko

"On the ball I think he's very good, off the ball he's strong" Enzo Maresca explains why he played Marc Guéhi in midfield in Manchester City's opening game against Bournemouth 🤔 pic.twitter.com/h4N1e1L8bf

"At home anything is possible" 💪Pierre Sage previews his sides clash with Manchester City at Selhurst Park 🔥 pic.twitter.com/oPJnZJVB6B

"He'll be very vital for us" 🔑Nico O'Reilly speaking about Manchester City's new signing Ayyoub Bouaddi ahead of their game against Crystal Palace 🔊 pic.twitter.com/2ptihsCY7c

There looks set to be a debut for the Premier League’s most expensive teenager off the visitors’ bench in the form of Ayyoub Bouaddi. There is no Jack Grealish in their squad as his future is up in the air.

Manchester City: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly, Anderson, Guehi, Cherki, Foden Semenyo, Haaland.Substitutes: Rulli, Kovacic, Ait-Nouri, Reis, Echeverri, Bouaddi, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Lewis.

Was it really just a year ago when Crystal Palace fans flooded down the Holmesdale Road with not a care in the world having just won the Community Shield to add to their FA Cup triumph over tonight’s opponents Manchester City? Well, they are marching along the Holmesdale Road in the same numbers again this evening, bedecked in red and blue as always, yet there is uncertainty and worry in the air and on their faces. Will the player exodus continue? What should they make of new manager Pierre Sage? Will the good times fade from view as quickly as they did for Leicester City or can Sage build a new side to match the one which, under Oliver Glasner, added the Conference League to their list of trophies three months ago?

“We struggled to get into the game and win the battles,” a disappointed Carlo Ancelotti lamented.

At the World Cup, an industrious 18-year-old showed maturity beyond his years to dominate the midfield against Ancelotti’s Brazil on his competitive international debut, earning Morocco a draw. That was, in fact, the second time an Ancelotti side had been undone by precocious teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Ancelotti’s remarks about losing the midfield battle are from after a Champions League match in October 2024, when Lille shocked Real Madrid to end their 36-game unbeaten run. Bouaddi was at the heart of both statement results for his club and country.

Tonight:Crystal Palace vs Manchester City

Saturday:Liverpool vs Nottingham ForestBournemouth vs EvertonCoventry vs Hull CityTottenham vs Newcastle

Sunday:Chelsea vs BrightonLeeds vs BrentfordSunderland vs FulhamManchester United vs Ipswich

Tonight's team to face Crystal Palace! ​​💪🩵XI | Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias (C), Gvardiol, O'Reilly, Anderson, Guéhi, Foden, Cherki, Semenyo, HaalandSUBS | Rulli, Kovačić, Aït-Nouri, Reis, Echeverri, Bouaddi, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Lewis🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/qNgJPXKDM7

The second weekend of the Premier League season kicks off under the lights in South London as Crystal Palace host Manchester City at Selhurst Park. Manchester City won both fixtures 3-0 last season and they are in fact unbeaten in their last 11 Premier league away games against Crystal Palace, who have won just two of the 22 top flight meetings.

Crystal Palace experienced defeat on the opening weekend, falling to a 2-0 loss at Everton last Saturday, meaning the Pierre Sage era started with a defeat. Tonight is Sage’s first home game in charge of the club.

“I think it will be a wonderful moment, but I prefer to have a wonderful moment with good news at the end of the game,” Sage said. “That is why I do not think about me in this situation. The most important thing is the team and the result for sure, because we prepare all the week for that, to make them [the fans] happy. They will be happy to see us, but I think they would prefer to see us win. I will give my life to make them happy. I cannot do more. When you are in this stadium [Selhurst Park], you feel the history. You feel that there is something heavy weighing on you. It is a great responsibility that I have been entrusted with. We cannot wait to see this stadium in action.”

Sage has confirmed that Ismaila Sarr, who has been linked with a move away from the club this summer, and Chadi Riad will miss out tonight due to injury, as will striker Jean-Philippe Mateta. Palace have confirmed the addition of Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and the French defender could be involved tonight.

Manchester City appeared to be heading towards defeat in Enzo Maresca’s first league game in charge of the club last weekend. They were 1-0 down at home against Bournemouth in the closing stages before goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol gave them a come-from-behind win.

It has been a busy week in the transfer window for Manchester City. Both Savio (formerly Savinho) and Omar Marmoush have left for Tottenham, joining a long list of departures from the Etihad this summer. Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi has arrived in an £85m deal from Lille and has become the most expensive teenager in Premier League history. Maresca has confirmed that 18-year-old Bouaddi is ready to start.

“He [Bouaddi] is ready,” Maresca said. “He was working with his former club so he is fit. We will see how long he needs in terms of adaptation but he is ready to go. He is quite calm. He does not look 18, he already looks older, which is important. But in this case, we need to go slowly because he is very young, he has come from a different country so there is no rush for him. He is going to help us now and in the future. He is very mature for being 18.”

Team news from Selhurst Park to follow shortly.

#2012. Andy Robertson set to scale Scotland’s Everest but King Kenny remains untouchable

Thursday is the 40th anniversary of Sir Kenny Dalglish winning his 102nd and final Scotland cap in a 3-0 win over Luxembourg at Hampden Park.

There was no formal announcement of a retirement afterwards. Paying a visit to the Dalglish family home in England, Andy Roxburgh asked the great man to help get him up and running as manager before focussing on his expanded role as player-boss of Liverpool.

At the age of 35, injuries were beginning to take hold and Dalglish had enough on his plate at Anfield without carrying the hopes of a nation on his shoulders as well. That night in November 1986 marked the end of the road.

It took four decades to reach a point where Andrew Robertson will match King Kenny’s record in Friday night’s Nations League game against North Macedonia. If he then plays against Switzerland on Monday he will move to 103 appearances and claim the crown as the most capped Scotland player of all time.

If someone has to topple the king then Robertson seems as good a candidate as any. Comparing players from different eras is always tricky and the Tottenham defender can do nothing about the fact that he plays in an age when players earn more caps than they did in the seventies or eighties.

Nor can he do anything about the fact that he plays left-back, a position which lacks the crowd wow of a goalscoring No.7 like Dalglish or John McGinn.

Brazil gave Cafu more games than Pele and if it’s good enough for the most successful nation in history, there should be no issue with Scotland handing more appearances to a full-back than we did to the most accomplished British attacker of all time. The achievement means the world to Robertson and his family and rightly so; they should savour the moment.

To children of the eighties like this one, the Dalglish cap haul felt like an Everest which would never be conquered; a record which never should be topped. Like retiring a shirt number in honour of a legendary player, it felt as if no one else should ever be allowed to surpass Scotland’s greatest player.

Kenny Dalglish (Image: Mark Leech/Offside)

Robertson would be the first to admit that the record will never make him the greatest Scotland player of all time because that’s a title which sticks with King Kenny. If Denis Law couldn’t pinch it, no one will.

Scoring 30 goals in dark blue and playing in three World Cups, Dalglish bore a talent which deserved that most overused of tags; that of the world-class player.

Not everyone thought so at the time, mind. Kenny was forever accused of performing better for Liverpool than he did for Scotland. Praise, and he received plenty, would be muttered through slightly gritted teeth.

The fulcrum in one of the greatest club sides of all time, he won six English league championships, three European Cups, an FA Cup, four League Cups and major honours as player-manager.

With Scotland, it was all about the moments. Rising to head home the goal against Wales which confirmed a place at the World Cup in Argentina. That quite magnificent individual strike against Belgium in 1982, his best, for me, and the thumping left-foot beauty against Spain in November 1984.

When he actually made it to the major tournaments, the dazzling smile which followed every goal was seen a little less than people would have liked. He struck in a memorable, if futile, win over the Dutch in 1978 and added another against New Zealand four years later.

For any player, scoring at back-to-back World Cup finals is a stamp of quality. His international goals total has only ever been matched by Law and, despite a valiant effort by John McGinn, that record will be harder to surpass than his cap tally.

If there is a ‘but’ attached to Kenny Dalglish, it’s the failure to lead the national team to the second stage of major international finals. Alas, the same asterisk can also be placed beside the name of Andrew Robertson.

John Clark's granddaughter opens up on bid to immortalise Lisbon Lion with statue

Ryan Jack knew Clement was doomed at Rangers as he reveals bad taste in his mouth

Morton may be struggling but charity is bringing hope to the community

Released by Celtic as a teenager for being too small, Robbo rebuilt his career at amateur Queen’s Park and then Dundee United, before winning two Premier League titles, a Champions League and a Club World Cup with Liverpool.

His nine years and 373 appearances at Anfield ended in the kind of tributes which feel like premature obituaries.

As an international player, he has driven the standards and culture which restored Scotland to two Euros and a first World Cup finals in 28 years.

It was Robertson’s idea to present players with personalised gift packs and handwritten notes before major tournaments.

On reaching the World Cup finals, his first thought was for his late Liverpool team-mate Diogo Jota.

Even if he never scores the kind of goals which make McGinn and Scott McTominay the darlings of the Tartan Army, his work rate, intensity and intelligence are the reasons managers love him and keep playing him.

Alex McLeish returned to manage the national team for a second time in February 2018 and made Robertson his skipper at the relatively young age of 24 after Scott Brown’s international retirement.

McLeish had won 77 caps over 13 years as a Scotland defender and knew what the role entailed. Describing Robertson as the ‘outstanding candidate’ and an ‘inspirational figure’, a leadership role at three major tournaments has vindicated that decision.

“By the end of this camp Andy should be above Kenny and I must be honest, I thought nobody would ever beat Kenny,” McLeish told Herald Sport.

Laughing, he adds: “It looks like Andy will and Kenny will be jealous of that.

“But I made Andy Scotland captain because he is a fantastic guy first and foremost.

“I could see that he was not scared to have a go at others and say, ‘hey, come on…’

“You need those qualities on the pitch and I think he is entitled to feel very proud of the footballer that he became after he joined Queen’s Park.

“He is a great fella, he has been a great captain, he has been a fantastic, ruthless winner in the club game as well. And, for me, Andy deserves everything that has come his way.”

Andy Robertson (right) in action for Scotland in 2014 (Image: Marcin Wziontek/Shutterstock)

The reality of professional football dictates that Robertson is 32 now and won’t be around much longer. The same might be said of McGinn and Ryan Christie and the group of players who have clawed Scotland back from the international wilderness.

When they go, it’s not clear who takes their place. Look at the under-21 team set to play Ukraine on Thursday and Aberdeen’s Mitchel Frame has played no first-team minutes this season. Bailey Rice of Kilmarnock has only managed 34 minutes since mid-September.

While the nation is still capable of producing proper players like Billy Gilmour, managers don’t seem to trust them enough to play first-team football.

Robertson derived the benefit of playing against men at an early age at Queen’s Park and then Dundee United and the same observation might be said of McGinn, Ryan Christie, Lewis Ferguson and Kieran Tierney. That’s how internationals are forged and right now the door is being slammed in the faces of the aspirational.

The lack of a first-team pathway for those aged between 16 and 21 is a ticking time bomb. A menace to the job prospects of Scotland managers of the future and of the here and now.

In a stark, if unsurprising, admission Sebastien Pocognoli spoke at the weekend of a lack of goalkeeper alternatives to Angus Gunn. Beyond Falkirk’s Scott Bain, Rangers reserve Liam Kelly and Jon McCracken, an English League One keeper, the cupboard is bare.

If the top clubs won’t play young players of their own accord, then they need to be incentivised or compelled to get their act together and, at a recent summit in St Andrews, SFA chief football officer Craig Mulholland unveiled a package of measures to address the situation.

Five top-flight teams need more persuasion over the plans, forcing Mulholland to tweak the details to reach a point where they might have some chance of being voted through.

If they won’t fly at all, then the SFA may have to consider the nuclear option. The governing body have the option of changing the rules to make it harder for clubs to secure Governing Body Endorsements, which are required for visas, for the Joel van den Bergs and Kosta Nedeljkovics of this world.

A points-based system, similar to that utilised in England, would separate the wheat from the chaff and compel clubs to get with the programme.

Andy Robertson knows better than anyone how hard it is for young Scots to make it at a club like Celtic. It took hard work, perseverance and talent to make it after an early rejection and for that reason alone Scotland fans should turn up at Hampden on Friday to salute the man on the cusp of claiming Sir Kenny’s caps record.

Debating which of the two deserves to be Scotland’s most capped footballer, then, obscures the bigger and more important point.

In both cases, the cream rose to the top and unless clubs get serious about fixing the current crisis in youth development, it could be some time before the nation sees their likes again.

#2010. ‘I want to…’ – Virgil van Dijk issues Liverpool contract hint as mega decision awaits

Virgil van Dijk has spoken about his long-term future at Liverpool, where he now has less than eight months remaining on his current contract.

Having penned a two-year extension in April 2025, the club captain is once again approaching a major crossroads in his illustrious career as the clock ticks towards the juncture at which a decision will have to be made.

Fellow stalwart Alisson Becker has voiced his desire to remain with the Reds beyond next summer, with his agent in ‘preliminary talks‘ over a potential new deal for the goalkeeper, although the Dutch defender has been rather more coy about his own situation.

Van Dijk addressed his long-term future when speaking to reporters after Liverpool’s 3-1 victory at Crystal Palace.

In quotes published by the Liverpool Echo on Tuesday, the 35-year-old said: “I feel good but it’s not about me at the moment. Let’s see. I’m not in any panic whatsoever. I want to keep playing and continue what I’m doing.

“Let’s see what the season brings. I’ve had an amazing time already so far. If that will be extended, that’s the case. If not, then I will go somewhere else. There’s nothing to report at the moment but that doesn’t mean that there’s any stress or anything.”

(Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Publicly at least, Van Dijk is giving nothing away about his future, with the Liverpool captain seemingly happy to stay on but also keeping his options open in case a new deal with the Reds can’t be agreed upon.

It’d certainly represent a break from the norm from Anfield chiefs to offer a lucrative contract extension to a player who’s already on £350,000 per week (Capology) and who’ll turn 36 next summer, but we’re not talking about any ordinary footballer here.

The captain is one of the greatest to ever pull on the iconic red shirt, and aside from an uncharacteristic error against Villarreal last month, he’s been imperious alongside Jeremy Jacquet at the heart of our defence this season.

The Frenchman is among several young centre-backs in line to ultimately succeed Van Dijk as our defensive general in the years to come (along with Giovanni Leoni and Ifeanyi Ndukwe), but the influence of the experienced Dutchman is still clear.

If the skipper’s preference would be to continue with Liverpool into next season, then hopefully he and the club can reach an agreement which’d keep him at Anfield beyond the end of this campaign.

#2005. How Celtic fans can apply for new engagement group after supporter feedback

Celtic have opened applications for supporters to join the club’s new fan engagement group, Celtic Connect.

The initiative is designed to strengthen communication between the Parkhead hierarchy and the support, with members of the group set to hold regular discussions with the club’s senior leadership.

Celtic had previously announced plans to establish Celtic Connect before undertaking a consultation period with supporters.

Following feedback, the club have now made several changes to their original proposal, including increasing membership from nine to 11 and introducing a place specifically for a match-going supporter who does not hold a season ticket.

Season ticket holders selected for the group will also come from across Celtic Park rather than being categorised by individual stands.

Meetings will now take place four times per year, while a three-year sliding membership structure will see a third of the group change annually in an attempt to balance continuity with the introduction of fresh voices.

Celtic say the group will discuss areas including the club's strategic vision and objectives, its heritage and history, supporter engagement, stadium development and the matchday experience.

The debrief on Celtic's Mika Baur worry, Haissem Hassan omission & familiar problems Kasper Hogh has Celtic goal ripped away but earns something just as telling

Applications are now open, with supporters given until Monday, November 23 to apply.

"We are delighted today to open the application process for our new Fan Engagement model, Celtic Connect.

"The Club had recently announced the intention to launch Celtic Connect and following a period of consultation, applications are now open to join the group.

"Celtic Football Club is committed to strengthening its relationship with supporters and ensuring that fans have a meaningful voice through this new structure. Celtic Connect will provide a forum for supporters to engage in regular discussions and liaison with the Club’s senior leadership.

"In arriving at a proposed structure and remit, we reviewed the approach taken by many clubs elsewhere in Britain, and took advice from other clubs on what works and doesn’t work, in order to learn from their experiences.

"Additionally, across the past few weeks during our consultation period we received some interesting and important feedback from supporters.

"We sincerely thank all those who provided feedback and following this process and our own review, we have made the following changes to the initial proposals.

"The Celtic Connect team will now be increased from 9 to 11 members.

"Season ticket holding representatives will be selected from right across the stadium and not categorised from particular stands as previously discussed.

"We have added a position for a non-season ticket holding, but match-attending supporter as part of the membership.

"Frequency of meetings has been updated to four times per year.

"We have introduced a three-year sliding scale in terms of membership so that a third of the group will change on an annual basis to ensure fresh voices but also continuity.

"Throughout the consultation process, it was also pleasing to receive significant interest from numerous supporters wishing to join the Celtic Connect team. We will be contacting all these supporters directly to ensure they have the opportunity to complete the relevant application process.

"As we have previously outlined, Celtic Connect will consider:

"The Club’s strategic vision and objectives;

"Any proposals relating to Celtic’s heritage and history;

"Further plans for broader supporter engagement;

"Matters relating to stadium development, matchday experience and projects associated with Celtic Park;

"Relevant information sharing between club and supporters.

"We thank our supporters for their interest and involvement in this process so far and we look forward to updating our fans further on the progress of Celtic Connect.

"We would encourage all supporters to consider applying to be part of the group. The closing date for applications is Monday, November 23, 2026."

#2004. 'Why are you speaking? F*** off!': Kevin De Bruyne at centre of Napoli dressing room meltdown as 'divided' squad lurches towards 'disaster'... with an 'every man for himself' culture setting in at Italian giants

Published: 03:23 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 05:08 EST, 6 November 2026

Kevin De Bruyne was told to 'f*** off' repeatedly during Napoli's 4-1 thrashing against Porto on Wednesday, with a dressing room crisis heating up at the club.

The Napoli squad has become increasingly fractured in recent weeks, according to the Italian media, with an 'every man for himself' culture developing into a 'disaster'.

Napoli sit eighth in Serie A under new manager Massimiliano Allegri – just two seasons after winning the title under Antonio Conte – and are near the bottom of the Champions League table after three defeats in four games.

Their cracks are showing on the pitch, with striker Lorenzo Lucca yelling at De Bruyne: 'Why are you speaking? F*** off!' during their Porto drubbing.

The pair squared up to each other and Lucca shouted his expletive command three times before they went their separate ways.

After the match, Matteo Politano told Sky Sport Italia: 'It would be nice if a few other teammates came here to give an explanation and not just us Italians, but never mind, I never hide my face.'

Kevin De Bruyne was told to 'f*** off' three times by team-mate Lorenzo Lucca during Napoli's 4-1 defeat by Porto on Wednesday

There is said to be a rift developing between Napoli's native stars and foreign players

La Gazzetta dello Sport reported that Politano was calling out Cameroonian star Frank Anguissa and Kosovan Amir Rrahmani, both two-time title winners with the club.

Politano added: 'The attitude is one that a team like ours cannot have at this level. I was not attacking anyone, we have a squad that is struggling, but we need to come together and think about this next game before the break for international duty.

'Hopefully we can recover a few players during that spell and then our season can really begin.'

There is a 'divide' between the Italian group of players and foreigners, La Gazzetta dello Sport reports, though it is mostly down to frustration with results.

Individuals such as De Bruyne, Rasmus Hojlund, and Stanislav Lobotka are more 'reserved personalities' who have reportedly not bonded as well with their team-mates away from the field.

Scott McTominay, who has an ally in fellow Scottish player Billy Gilmour, said after the Porto loss: 'Of course I’m angry.

'We lost 4-1 in the Champions League; there’s nothing to smile about. For us, it’s go on and try to figure out how to fix it.

'We’ve had a lot of injuries, a lot of important players you can’t change; attacking players as well. Let’s not beat around the bush; we’ve got a lot of injuries, and that makes a big difference whenever you come into play every three days.

Napoli have had a rough start to the season under new manager Massimiliano Allegri - despite him being a legendary coach in Italy

'So, things like these can make a huge difference for the team when the same players are playing over and over again. People need to understand that, but we also need to do better. First and foremost, we need to do better, injuries in football are part of it, but we have too many.'

Their dressing room troubles have dragged on for a while. Last season, Conte complained of a lack of unity after they signed nine players on the back of their Scudetto. They still managed to finish second, but it was a turbulent ride.

'Nine new players were too many. We weren't balanced,' he said at the time.

'I experience the dressing room every day, so I say certain things; we mustn't despair. We'll try to recreate last year's chemistry.'

In one match against AC Milan, De Bruyne threw a tantrum after being subbed off by Conte.

#2003. Bayern won’t sign Rio Ngumoha after missing their chance in the summer – opinion

Bayern Munich are reportedly confident that there is a deal to be done with Liverpool for talented youngster Rio Ngumoha.

The Reds were understood to be the subject of some probing from the Bavarian giants, with discussions said to have taken place with the winger’s brother.

Whether Liverpool feel the same way… well, let’s just be clear on this: they don’t.

As Mick Brown noted in his latest report with Football Insider: “From what I hear, Bayern Munich are pretty confident there is a deal to be done.

“When there’s all this talk about making contact with his agents, speaking to the player, what it might cost, that stuff doesn’t happen unless they think they can do a deal.

“Whether Liverpool feel the same way, I have my doubts, because he has such obvious potential and Andoni Iraola has been pretty clear he is part of his plans.

“I don’t think he’s the finished article, but not many players are at 18, there are still areas of his game where he has to improve, so maybe that’s where the speculation comes from.”

Mick goes on to note that the Reds are currently giving Ngumoha everything he could realistically hope for at an elite European outfit. There is a pathway to the senior team and he’s already picked up 642 minutes (Transfermarkt) of action in the famous red shirt this season.

On top of that, his all-round game is being carefully developed, with appearances roughly split between both flanks.

And most importantly? Liverpool aren’t burning the player out — Andoni Iraola is managing the teenager’s minutes, rotating alongside Bradley Barcola, Victor Munoz and Cody Gakpo.

So, Bayern may feel a deal can be done, but realistically, can they offer the 18-year-old substantially more than he’s already receiving at Liverpool?

It’s worth pointing out that, as is indeed the case across Europe’s biggest outfits, Bayern’s shortlist is far from limited to Liverpool’s No.73. Names like Antonio Nusa and Oskar Pietuszewski are also highly rated by the club, with the former thought to be well-admired by Bayern chief Max Eberl.

But the important distinction to make here is that Ngumoha will not come cheap – far from it, compared to the two names alone we’ve just listed. And if Bayern already valued the versatile winger at €70m [£58.3m] in the summer, can you imagine how much his value has skyrocketed since becoming an important part of Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool squad? We’re surely talking in the territory of at least upwards of £7om, at a conservative estimate.

On that basis, options like Pietuszewski – who reportedly has a €60m [£50.1m] release clause at FC Porto – surely start to look more feasible for a club like Bayern that doesn’t necessarily have the same level of cash to splash as its Premier League counterparts.

#2001. Celtic board urge AGM rejection of 3 major shareholder demands including full apology

Celtic chiefs have urged shareholders to vote down a trio of proposals ahead of this year’s AGM.

Shareholders will gather at Celtic Park on December 1, with the board recommending they reject three of the four shareholder requisitions.

The meeting comes against a backdrop of discontent and unrest among sections of the Celtic support, with fan groups urging principal shareholder Dermot Desmond to attend.

And three of the resolutions set to go before shareholders cut to the heart of the current tensions surrounding the club.

The first calls on Celtic to undertake a full strategic review and publish a football, financial and strategic plan.

Interim chairman Brian Wilson has insisted work is already under way to modernise Celtic and address areas requiring improvement. However, the board will stop short of agreeing to the full review being demanded.

Read more: How Celtic fans can apply for new engagement group after supporter feedback

A second resolution calls for a full review of security operations at Celtic Park amid the continuing breakdown in relations between the club and the Green Brigade.

The ultras have been at loggerheads with the hierarchy over how they believe they have been treated, with relations souring further following a flashpoint last season which resulted in the group being banned after an incident involving police officers during the clash with Falkirk.

The third proposal demands that Celtic’s chairman issue a “full and unreserved apology” to shareholders and supporters.

But that was always set to be a non-starter. While the club acknowledges work has to be done, the board are urging shareholders to reject the call for an apology.

This year’s gathering also arrives 12 months on from a stormy AGM which saw Ross Desmond, son of principal shareholder Dermot, hit back at critics over the running of Celtic moments before then-chairman Peter Lawwell called time on proceedings.

#1998. Scotland hero tells Pocognoli the change Tartan Army are desperate to see

Robert Snodgrass reckons Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli should tap into the country's love affair with flying wingers as he continues to mould the national team in his image.

The former Scotland star accepts Pocognoli needs time to impose his ideas after succeeding Steve Clarke and believes the work between international camps will be crucial.

Pocognoli has favoured a 3-4-1-2 during the opening four games of his reign, a system which leaves little room for two out-and-out wingers. But Snodgrass would love to see Scotland eventually find a way of getting genuine wide men into the team and believes it could provide the attacking spark the Tartan Army crave.

Snodgrass, speaking to BOYLE Sports, who offer football odds, said: “It was a big decision him coming in. He hasn't started so well that people are completely sold on the formation and style giving immediate hope or suitability for the squad. That's the general feeling coming back from the first camp.

Read more: Next Aberdeen manager odds as frontunners emerge after Stephen Robinson sacked

“But he needs time to implement his ideas.

“A lot of international managers say they don't get enough time on the grass in international football.

“During the gaps between camps, your analysts need to reach out to players and share work. Take the time to meet up with key players, your right-backs, wingers, strikers, and go through the footage so that when the squad meets up, you're not starting from scratch.

“Meet them, show them the work and get these fresh ideas into their mindsets. They might already be doing that behind the scenes.

“When you step into the job, the workload increases as you try to get players comfortable with new concepts.

“When people feel an uncomfortable change, you have to put the work in so the lads feel it's simple, know their roles and believe in what we're trying to achieve. Once that happens, it creates belief within the squad that we're heading in the right direction.”

Snodgrass believes Pocognoli already has a solid platform to work from after the Clarke era. But the former winger naturally wants to see Scotland add another dimension higher up the pitch.

He added: “Momentum and positivity are key for Scotland. When they're in a good flow, you know Scotland will always be in games.

“They aren't expansive to the point of leaving themselves wide open, but are built off a solid base.

“That's a good starting point, but as confidence grows, I'd like to see us play with out-and-out wingers. They have Gannon-Doak, Josh McPake, lads who can go one-v-one and cause problems. I'd love to see that.

“It creates a spark and an atmosphere that Scotland fans are desperate for.

“We're used to good wingers in Scottish football. Being a winger myself, I might sound biased, but who doesn't want to see exciting, attacking football for Scotland?

“Steve Clarke built a strong defensive base, and the next challenge for the manager is to build on that by adding a real attacking style with players who can cause teams serious problems.”

And Snodgrass has a clear idea of who should be leading that attack.

Kieron Bowie has impressed and strengthened his case during the early stages of Pocognoli's reign, but Snodgrass reckons Oli McBurnie remains Scotland's best option through the middle.

McBurnie hasn't provided a glut of goals, but his performances across Pocognoli's opening four-game run appear to have changed the conversation around his international prospects.

Snodgrass said: “Oli McBurnie has proved he can score goals everywhere he's been. He's a great lad to have around the place, has matured a lot and has experience leading the line in the Premier League.

“Even in that game down to ten men against Switzerland, his performance was excellent. He showed everyone what he brings.

“In Scotland, we love a big number nine who can hold the ball up, attack crosses and link play. He has a lot in his armoury, so we need to stick with him.

“I feel for Bowie and the other young forwards, but having them come off the bench is a great option.

“Right now, leading the line in the Premier League gives Oli the edge, but Bowie and the others aren't far behind. They're three great attacking options for Scotland.

“They tried two up top, but it takes a few camps to realise what your best setup is.”
